classification.difficultyReason: Each part links routine quadratic intersections, a sketch, upper-boundary selection and definite integration using the explicitly taught procedure.

content.prompt: Solve simultaneously, sketch, shade the enclosed region, and find its area for:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-6x+5&=x-5\\x^2-7x+10&=0\\(x-2)(x-5)&=0\\x&=2\text{ or }x=5\end{aligned}$$
Intersections: $(2,-3)$ and $(5,0)$. The line is above the parabola on $[2,5]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_2^5\big((x-5)-(x^2-6x+5)\big)\,dx\\&=\int_2^5(7x-10-x^2)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{7x^2}{2}-10x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_2^5\\&=\left(\frac{175}{2}-50-\frac{125}{3}\right)-\left(14-20-\frac83\right)\\&=-\frac{25}{6}-\left(-\frac{26}{3}\right)\\&=\frac92\text{ units}^2\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}-3x&=4-x^2\\x^2-3x-4&=0\\(x-4)(x+1)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }x=-1\end{aligned}$$
Intersections: $(4,-12)$ and $(-1,3)$. The parabola is above the line on $[-1,4]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-1}^4\big((4-x^2)-(-3x)\big)\,dx\\&=\int_{-1}^4(4+3x-x^2)\,dx\\&=\left[4x+\frac{3x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^4\\&=\left(16+24-\frac{64}{3}\right)-\left(-4+\frac32+\frac13\right)\\&=\frac{56}{3}-\left(-\frac{13}{6}\right)\\&=\frac{125}{6}\text{ units}^2\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-1&=7-x^2\\2x^2&=8\\x^2&=4\\x&=2\text{ or }x=-2\end{aligned}$$
Intersections: $(2,3)$ and $(-2,3)$. The second curve is above the first on $[-2,2]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-2}^2\big((7-x^2)-(x^2-1)\big)\,dx\\&=\int_{-2}^2(8-2x^2)\,dx\\&=\left[8x-\frac{2x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^2\\&=\left(16-\frac{16}{3}\right)-\left(-16+\frac{16}{3}\right)\\&=\frac{32}{3}+\frac{32}{3}\\&=\frac{64}{3}\text{ units}^2\end{aligned}$$
